decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out in `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787` (`//#define MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`). | WHY: The answer states only that MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is commented out in the header. It never says MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD is also undefined in the shipped config, and it says the index's THREADING_PTHREAD was "set by flag for this build". || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out in `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787` (`//#define MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`). | WHY: The answer states only that MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is commented out in the shipped header; it never says the second threading macro (PTHREAD/ALT) is also undefined, and it mentions THREADING_ALT and THREADING_PTHREAD only as an index build flag and an alternative, not as defaults. || QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out in `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787` (`//#define MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`). | WHY: The answer states only that MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is undefined by default. It never says the shipped header leaves MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD undefined, so one of the two macros is missing.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The library spawns no threads. The four spawn sites the index found are all in `programs/`... Every mutex use in `library/` sits behind `#if defined(MBEDTLS_THREADING_C)`. That includes `threading.c` itself... The lock functions are function pointers (`threading.c`), defaulting to pthread. `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` replaces them. | WHY: The answer states that the library spawns no threads, and that library/ supplies the mutex abstraction (threading.c with pluggable lock function pointers, global mutexes) for threaded callers. || QUOTE: The library spawns no threads.
